Usage: mdg [options] [command]

MDG (Markdown Graph): inspect, edit and validate recursive message-flow
architecture documents (.mdg).

Options:
  -V, --version                                 output the version number
  -h, --help                                    display help for command

Commands:
  info [options] <file>                         Show document summary: title, versions, root, counts and file size.
  tree [options] <file>                         Show the module hierarchy.
  describe [options] <file> <module-id>         Describe a module as Markdown. Depth 0 shows the public contract only; depth 1 adds children and internal connections; depth N recurses N levels. Only the needed Markdown is read.
  inputs [options] <file> <module-id>           List a module's inputs with their Markdown contracts.
  outputs [options] <file> <module-id>          List a module's outputs with their Markdown contracts.
  connections [options] <file> <module-id>      List the connections inside a module's internal graph.
  trace [options] <file> <module-id> <port-id>  Trace possible structural message routes from a port across parent boundaries. Routes do not imply runtime execution order.
  validate [options] <file>                     Check structural validity. Exits 1 when errors exist; warnings do not fail by default.
  export [options] <file>                       Export documentation for the entire hierarchy.
  new [options] <file>                          Create a new document containing only a root module.
  module                                        Add, remove, rename, move or describe modules.
  port                                          Add, remove, rename or describe ports.
  connect [options] <file> <from> <to>          Connect two ports (directed message flow). Endpoints are <module-id>:<port-id>. Without --route both ports must be on the same hierarchy level. With --route, boundary ports and local connections are created at every intermediate level.
  disconnect [options] <file> <connection-id>   Remove a connection by ID.
  help [command]                                display help for command

Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 validation errors / rejected edit, 2 usage error,
            3 file or format error, 4 module/port/connection not found.

Examples:
  $ mdg tree architecture.mdg --ids
  $ mdg describe architecture.mdg api-service --depth 1
  $ mdg connect architecture.mdg a:out b:in --route --dry-run
  $ mdg validate architecture.mdg --json

Usage: mdg module [options] [command]

Add, remove, rename, move or describe modules.

Options:
  -h, --help                                    display help for command

Commands:
  add [options] <file>                          Add a module under a parent.
  remove [options] <file> <module-id>           Remove a module. Fails if it has children or connections unless --cascade is given.
  rename [options] <file> <module-id> <name>    Rename a module. Its ID never changes.
  move [options] <file> <module-id>             Move a module (and its subtree) under a new parent. IDs are preserved; moves that would invalidate connections are rejected.
  set-description [options] <file> <module-id>  Replace a module's Markdown description.
  help [command]                                display help for command

Usage: mdg connect [options] <file> <from> <to>

Connect two ports (directed message flow). Endpoints are <module-id>:<port-id>.
Without --route both ports must be on the same hierarchy level. With --route,
boundary ports and local connections are created at every intermediate level.

Arguments:
  file                     .mdg file
  from                     source endpoint <module-id>:<port-id>
  to                       destination endpoint <module-id>:<port-id>

Options:
  --id <id>                explicit connection ID (local connections only)
  --container <module-id>  module whose internal graph stores the connection
                           (inferred by default)
  --route                  route across hierarchy levels through generated
                           boundary ports
  --via <module:port...>   with --route: use this existing boundary port at
                           that module
  --no-reuse               with --route: never reuse existing boundary ports
  --output-name <name>     with --route: name for generated output ports
  --input-name <name>      with --route: name for generated input ports
  --json                   machine-readable result
  --dry-run                validate and report the change without writing the
                           file
  -h, --help               display help for command

Examples:
  $ mdg connect architecture.mdg frontend:login-submitted api-service:login-request
  $ mdg connect architecture.mdg protected-endpoint:token-check jwt-validator:validate-token --route --dry-run --json
